breaking.headline: Dow erases a 1,100-point plunge to hold 50,000 into Thanksgiving
breaking.fact: The Dow fell more than 1,100 points Wednesday morning before closing up 164.25 at 50,182.95, while the S&P 500 fell 3.2% intraday and closed down just 0.25% at 7,182.78 and the Nasdaq fell 4.6% before closing down 0.62%. U.S. futures are higher in thin Thanksgiving trade, with the S&P up about 0.7%.

breaking.headline: HP jumps 11% on earnings beat, dividend hike and a new CEO
breaking.fact: HP shares rose 11% Wednesday to $30.88 after fiscal fourth-quarter revenue grew 9.3% to $16 billion, beating estimates, with AI PCs reaching nearly 60% of shipments. The company raised its quarterly dividend to $0.31, its 11th straight annual increase, and former GSK chief Emma Walmsley takes over as CEO on January 4.

breaking.headline: Gold stages a V-shaped rebound from a 14-month low
breaking.fact: Spot gold fell below $3,450 an ounce Wednesday, its lowest in more than a year, before recovering to $3,576.30 as Treasury yields eased and tech stocks stabilized; silver rebounded to $41.12. Gold traded above $3,600 again Thursday morning as safe-haven demand returned.

breaking.headline: Copper jumps 3.4% in a short-covering rebound from an 11-month low
breaking.fact: Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange jumped more than 3% to $12,047 a ton Thursday, rebounding from its lowest since December 2025 as tech stocks recovered and crowded shorts unwound. Copper is still down about 15% in November, and all six LME base metals rose in thin Thanksgiving trade.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide's Paris quote stands at €189.92 from Wednesday's close, worth $207.68 at the ECB's Nov 25 reference rate of 1.0935, up 0.8% in dollars. Paris traded through the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday while American markets sat out, so the chip's dollar price tracks the euro into Friday's half session. The industrial-gas giant keeps grinding higher as tech gives back its rally.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic closed Wednesday at $82.79, up 1.1% as the stock steadied just below its $83 IPO price after a choppy first week of trading. The AI lab behind Claude is still the talk of the math world after its Nov 20 Riemann proof, certified by the Lean community, and a Navier-Stokes claim the same day. With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving, the next test comes in Friday's thin half session.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up a penny Wednesday to $91.64, the quiet government-cash anchor doing its job while growth stocks sold off and the VIX spiked to 28.29. Its distribution yield sits at 4.04%, with the latest payout of $0.30849 per share paid Nov 5. In a week when the Nasdaq fell 4.6% intraday before recovering, the Treasury-bill fund's steadiness is the whole point. The fund's yield tracks the Fed's path closely.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet fell 2.1% Wednesday to $273.10, giving back more of the week's gains as the Nasdaq slid 0.6% and chip stocks led the selloff. The drop came with no company-specific news, as hot PCE data pushed December hike odds near 95% and pressured rate-sensitive growth names. Futures point higher into Friday's half session, but the stock needs tech sentiment to stabilize before the slide finds a floor.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly slipped 1.1% Wednesday to $1,392.22, a modest pullback after Tuesday's 3.2% jump as money rotated toward defensive names and away from growth. The drugmaker held up far better than the Nasdaq, which fell 4.6% intraday before recovering most of the drop. With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving, Lilly's next move waits on Friday's thin half session and whether the safety rotation keeps running.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere Energy jumped 2.0% Wednesday to $301.99, showing steady strength while oil whipsawed and the market fell apart intraday. Brent crude settled up 3.5% at $94.61 after Houthi strikes on Saudi ports, and U.S. LNG exporters keep benefiting from tight global gas markets. With energy the day's outperformer and Gulf tensions still rising, Cheniere's run looks more durable than a one-day bounce.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia fell 3.9% Wednesday to $149.30, giving back more of Monday's 31% surge after Huang's reinstatement, and S&P then put its AA rating on CreditWatch Negative over governance risks. The agency cited the CEO's 12-day exit and return and questions over board oversight, with a downgrade possible in 90 days. Futures point higher for Friday, but the credit watch adds a fresh overhang to a stock already under scrutiny.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer was flat Wednesday at $28.46, holding Tuesday's 3.9% gain as investors rotated into defensive dividend payers during the market's wild intraday swing. The drugmaker's steadiness stood out while the Nasdaq plunged 4.6% before recovering and the VIX spiked to 28.29. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, Pfizer's dividend yield keeps it on the safe-haven list heading into Friday's half session.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab jumped 2.3% Wednesday to $47.02, bouncing with the market's late-day recovery after Tuesday's 7.4% slide. The space stock remains one of the tape's most volatile names, swinging hard with risk appetite as the Nasdaq fell 4.6% intraday before clawing most of it back. No company news drove the move — it was pure sentiment — so Friday's thin half session could bring another sharp swing either way.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital rose 2.9% Wednesday to $8.92, extending a strong week as the mortgage REIT's dividend yield drew buyers during the market's flight to income. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.85% as stocks recovered from their intraday lows, a friendly backdrop for mortgage REITs. With a December Fed hike now priced near 95%, the rate path matters more than ever for Rithm's book value and payout.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SPCX, the leveraged S&P 500 fund, rose 1.3% Wednesday to $127.44, tracking the market's late recovery with its usual amplified swing. The S&P fell 3.2% intraday before closing down just 0.25%, so the leveraged fund's gain reflects the furious afternoon buying rather than a calm day. Futures point higher into Friday, but leveraged funds cut both ways — a thin half session could magnify any move.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist Financial rose 0.9% Wednesday to $47.89, holding up as the Dow climbed above 50,000 for the first time and banks caught a bid in the late recovery. Financials benefited as the 10-year yield held near 4.85% and the market priced a December hike as near-certain. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, Truist's next test is Friday's half session and whether the Dow can hold its round-number milestone.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony rose 1.4% Wednesday to $2.21, steadying after Tuesday's 8.8% slide as small miners sold off. China's export curbs and U.S. critical-mineral policy remain the long-term bull case, but the stock trades with the market's risk appetite day to day. The Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge and recovery set the tone; with futures higher into Friday, the antimony miner could keep steadying if sentiment holds.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy rose 2.2% Wednesday to $5.69, recovering part of Tuesday's 4.6% slide in the market's late rebound. Nuclear expansion and U.S. uranium buying remain the structural story, but the stock is tied to risk appetite while the Fed's rate path dominates the tape. With oil jumping on Gulf tensions and futures pointing higher for Friday, the setup favors a steadier session if the thin holiday market cooperates.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: VI5TC is estimated at $147.64, down 0.3% on the S&P 500's Wednesday slide, using the S&P-anchored estimator recalibrated from Dave's account value. The S&P fell as much as 3.2% intraday before closing down just 0.25%, so the estimate reflects the close, not the panic low. With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving and futures pointing higher, the next estimate comes after Friday's half session.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero Energy slipped 0.5% Wednesday to $323.00 even as the Dow hit 50,000, as oil seesawed and refiners gave back gains. Brent settled up 3.5% at $94.61 after Houthi strikes on Saudi ports and a refinery, a mixed picture for refiners: higher crude lifts product prices but squeezes margins. With Gulf tensions still rising and oil trading higher Thursday, Valero's direction hinges on how far the supply scare runs.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: The Target Retirement 2035 fund's NAV edged up to $28.45 as of Nov 25, a small gain as stocks recovered from intraday lows in the late session. The balanced fund's bond sleeve cushioned the Nasdaq's 4.6% intraday plunge, while its equity holdings joined the afternoon rebound. With markets closed for Thanksgiving, the next NAV prints after Friday's half session, when the fund will price a thin, holiday-shortened tape.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: SWVXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Schwab's 7-day SEC yield at 3.79% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The sweep fund keeps doing its quiet job while the market whipsaws — the VIX spiked to 28.29 Wednesday and the Nasdaq fell 4.6% intraday before recovering. Per the standing plan, balances above $1,000 get swept into CDs, so the position should keep shrinking toward zero over time.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: VUSXX holds its $1.00 NAV, with Vanguard's 7-day SEC yield at 4.01% as published Nov 25, unchanged from the prior reading. The Treasury money fund remains the top-yielding cash parking spot on the board, comfortably ahead of Schwab's SWVXX at 3.79%. With markets closed for Thanksgiving and a December hike priced near 95%, money-fund yields should stay firm into Friday's half session and beyond.

weekInBrief.headline: Houthi strikes on Saudi ports and a refinery lift oil sharply
weekInBrief.body: Yemen's Houthis claimed drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and the ports of Jeddah and Jazan, and the Saudi-led coalition said a projectile caused minor damage at Jazan. Brent crude settled up 3.5% at $94.61 a barrel on Wednesday and WTI rose 2.0% to $83.68, with both trading higher again in thin Thanksgiving sessions as traders priced in supply-disruption risk.

weekInBrief.headline: Markets now price a December Fed hike as near-certain
weekInBrief.body: Futures markets put a quarter-point December rate hike at 94–96% after October core PCE came in hot at 3.3% and third-quarter GDP was revised up to 4.3%, the fastest in three years. It would be a sharp turn from the easing path markets expected this fall, and the pricing held even as stocks staged a historic intraday reversal on Wednesday.

weekInBrief.headline: Bitcoin rebounds above $61,000, but ETF outflows deepen
weekInBrief.body: Bitcoin climbed back above $61,000 on Thursday, up about 2.5% in a day, as crypto joined the global rebound from Wednesday's selloff. The recovery came even as spot Bitcoin ETFs shed another $453 million in 24 hours, extending a seven-day outflow streak to $2.5 billion, a sign institutions are still pulling money despite the bounce.

weekInBrief.headline: Trump says Iran campaign funded 'through January' as strikes weighed
weekInBrief.body: President Trump told the New York Post the U.S. military campaign against Iran remains funded “through January,” and NBC News reported administration officials are weighing strikes on senior Iranian leaders. The comments came as the U.S. blockade of Iranian oil enters its fifth month, with Gulf tensions keeping oil prices elevated into the holiday.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Iran has not loaded a single oil tanker since Operation Economic Outcast began in August, and trackers noted the first tanker observed loading at Kharg Island since September — though no Iranian crude tanker has evaded the blockade since July 14. Iran’s army claimed it shot down two U.S. drones, an MQ-9 and a second aircraft, and its Strait Authority added 26 tugboats to its non-compliance blacklist, now 266 vessels. No Iranian oil is getting past the blockade: Treasury says not a single tanker has loaded since August and Kpler still puts Iranian loadings at zero, while CENTCOM says Gulf partners shipped a record 108 million barrels of crude through the strait under U.S. protection last week, the largest weekly volume yet.

space.headline: AI-aided team claims the 'real' Navier-Stokes proof — with a catch
space.body: Anthropic's Levent Alpöge and NYU's Tristan Buckmaster say they have proved finite-time blow-up for the unforced 3D Navier-Stokes equations, closing the loophole in OpenAI's September result, which relied on an artificial external force. The 79-page paper and Lean formalization were posted Nov 20, but the numerical certificate that completes the proof has not yet been released, so the claim is unverified for now.

space.headline: Ocean iodine won't rescue air quality as seas warm, study finds
space.body: A University of York study in Science Advances finds marine iodine emissions will dip about 3% by 2100 instead of surging as earlier models assumed, because warmer seas slow the release of iodine gas that destroys ground-level ozone. Iodine now accounts for nearly 11% of ozone destruction, falling to 10.2% by century’s end — bad news for air quality, though Arctic iodine emissions are projected to surge 143% as sea ice retreats.

space.headline: Europa's vast sodium cloud stays stable across decades
space.body: Seven observing epochs from 1999 to 2025 show Europa's distant sodium cloud barely changes, even as the moon moves through Jupiter's wildly varying plasma environment. The Keck I observations found sodium abundance beyond 20 Europa radii varied by less than a factor of two, far steadier than earlier models spanning a factor of five — suggesting slow transport blurs the link between local plasma conditions and the distant cloud.

space.headline: Hubble maps 25 million stars to sharpen Roman's planet hunt
space.body: NASA published new Hubble images of the Milky Way’s galactic bulge on Nov 25, a precursor survey of the fields the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will watch for microlensing events starting in spring 2027. The planned catalog of about 25 million stars will let astronomers turn Roman’s planet-to-star mass ratios into actual planet masses — the missing piece a light curve alone cannot give.

apod.title: Seeking Refuge on Resolution Island
apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey
apod.explanation: Resolution Island, in Fiordland on New Zealand’s South Island, was eyed as a predator-free refuge for native birds as early as 1872 — but stoats proved able to swim there. This Landsat 9 image from December 12, 2025, shows the uninhabited island rising to Mount Clerke at 1,069 meters amid steep glacial valleys now filled by the sea, where a conservation program has worked since 2008 to control stoats and bolster kiwi and kākāpō.
